《Rogue Monster Rush》是一款十分小巧却很有趣的肉鸽塔防作品，不同于传统肉鸽建造+放塔的传统模式，本作结合了地块构筑这一独特的玩法，把敌人的波次变为有玩家连接岛屿而进攻的可控模式，让塔防的体验充满未知与肉鸽的乐趣，每一次挑战都是全新的地图，十分适合想要体验独特塔防玩法的朋友。 游戏和一般的塔防游戏区别还是很大的，传统塔防一般是固定的地图，固定波次的结构模式。而本作则需要玩家通过搭建一个个岛屿把基地链接到boss老巢，并且每一次连接岛屿都会刷新新的波次，这就会让本身的防线越来越长，而且在每次开始游戏时还会在海面上随机刷新一些岛屿上，这些岛屿可能会有一些能强化精灵的宝箱以及一些随机精灵蛋，需要玩家巧妙的把这些岛屿连接到你的建筑路线上才能获取这些收益。 不过话说回来，作为一款塔防作品本作的防御塔种类在此类游戏中算十分少的那一种，游戏中的防御塔是各种类似神奇宝贝的精灵构成，但仅有十种左右的不同精灵，诸如什么火球怪、仙人掌怪等等，看起来丑萌丑萌的，好在每一位角色都有三个等级区分，并且每一种精灵都可以学习七八种不同的技能来进行配合，因此还是有一定的策略性的。 此外在游戏的玩法上由于加入了地块拼接，导致每一波怪物的出现战线拉的都会更长，塔防的摆布也很难集中，而是变成了分区域的摆放方式，而且针对这种战场变化的玩法模式，本作也为玩家提供了便利的防御塔移动方式，只需要缴纳一点点金币就可以自由移动防御塔，变更战略重心地点。 目前游戏一共有四种不同的难度和四块不同的挑战地形，除了最开始简单的草地以外还有冻原、森林这些难度更高的关卡，而游戏本身的难度并不低，即便是普通难度都有着一定的挑战性，所以对于喜欢塔防且热爱挑战的玩家，本作是个不错的选择。 [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

This is a great little game in a slick package of polish and presentation. It somehow feels both modern and nostalgic at the same time. Gameplay clarity, status effects, and other important information are all very clear (except for the lava biome), which can be a challenge for this genre. The monsters/units are cute and distinct from one another, and the deep upgrades and customization options are mechanically interesting and keep runs feeling fresh. The tile placement and restrictions on units per tile add some nice tactical variety and strategy to the mix, and overall the pacing and build up of each run feels great. My only real criticism has less to do with what the game is, and more to do with what it marketed itself as. I kind of got sold on this idea of Pokemon + TD + Roguelite but the monster taming/capture is really just a light thematic wrapper around what other TDs would just consider Tower upgrades. And the Roguelite elements are probably the weakest part of the game, where the only variance comes from mid-Run monster upgrades where there is usually a mathematically best choice that just increases stats. I just picked the highest rarity option, and/or the upgrade for whatever monster I had built most up to that point. Discovering the eggs and placing different island tiles were neat but they hardly justify calling this game a roguelite. That said, regardless of what the game was touted as being, it ended up being a well polished, tightly scoped little package of a game, and I plan on putting in another 10 hours or more before I call it a day.

Great fun tower defense. Lots of little doods to unlock and they all feel decently unique. Its a joy unlocking a new monster and trying to find some excuse to use it with a new team and I love the looks of every monsters evolution. There are only 4 maps but each one is definitely unique in the way you have to build around the mechanics: like the second map is effectively a mob rush that can be stopped with tank killers or by whittling them down with aoe attacks. The hatchery idea is neat, but frankly it is kind of grindy when you can only hatch one egg at a time withing roughly 7ish waves of a map. I am super excited for an endless mode though, but by then I still wont have all the monsters unlocked. Really though Rogue Monster Rush is a ton of fun and even if it is not the hardest tower defense game, it makes up for with how simple it is to set up a new team comp just for funsies rather than worrying about winning.

It has been a long time since I was grabbed so much by a tower defense game! "Rogue Monster Rush" at first sight seemed a bit ... weird, but soon proved to has much content to offer and much motivation to gift for some hours of descent fun, because ... + it has monsters instead of towers which adds to the lovely gameplay a lot + an unfolding map instead of strict pathes - every wave you decide which part of the world becomes larger + a lot of tactic involved when paying attention to synergies, which is at least necessary from medium difficulty upwards Overall, I have fun with "Rogue Monster Rush", and that's all I demand from a game. And I highly recommend clicking tier 2 of the abilities very soon to discover an FPS minigun to use when your monsters are simply overpowered. And belive me, they will be :) !

Every time I started a game, it acted as if it was getting a joystick input moving the screen to the top left making the game unplayable. I unplugged everything but my mouse and keyboard. Even disabled bluetooth, the game was still getting a joystick input. After hours of troubleshooting and uninstalling everything I could think of, I found that I needed to uninstall my 3DConnexion Spacemouse driver. Just having the mouse off and the bluetooth connection disabled did not help. A full uninstall of the driver was the only thing that got rid of the fake joystick input in this game. The game itself is really fun.

This is a great game, unfortunately there are three massive issues that make it not worth the purchase. 1. Broken Achievements - There are multiple achievements that are just straight up broken, you cannot get them. The worst is the "Defeat a boss without using player abilities" which I have tried doing full runs on hard without abilities and not gotten. 2. Egg Progression - You have an xp limit to unlock an egg which is about 1/8 what you get for a full hard mode run. This makes it so the incentive is to play a few waves then surrender because earning more xp is pointless. It doesn't overcap to unlock more eggs at once it's one then you have to quit the run, open the egg, then start a new run. 3. Single Mon Spam - The best strategy that works on all maps and all difficulties is the base mon sprout, you can take only sprout and 1 other mon in your party then only use sprout and beat maps with no difficulty at all. It apparently works with other mons but sprout has multi-shot upgrades and is the easiest.

[i]---see where this game landed on my tower defense tier list beneath this rec!---[/i] This is a pretty well done tower defense with [i]some[/i] similarities to [b]PokePath TD[/b]. It's a very grindy and repetitive TD, where at some point you will probably get like me and be like "well that was good, but I'm done with the repetition". I should point out that this is not an idler like [b]PokePath[/b], which was that games way of making the grind and repetition accessable to some. This games way of trying to make the grind more interesting is by going heavy on the rogue[b]lite[/b] aspect. With each run you earn currency to upgrade your creatures, spells and other things. Once you max out a creatures upgrades, you can choose to evolve them, with makes them a tiny bit stronger and removes all of the upgrades you had spent on them, causing you to need to improve them again. For the first few hours at least, this works for me and seeing my spells and creatures get more powerful each run was quite fun. There aren't many creatures (I think 16?), however I felt deterred from switching my team up, because the upgrades I had already put into my current team would've then felt like a waste. It's enough time and effort strengthening one team, so trying to improve all of the other creatures at the same time seemed like a daunting and tedious endeavor. The progression, whilst fun for a while does ultimately feel flawed longer-term. I like the audio (the sounds more than the music), though the sound effects are a bit loud compared to the music on the default settings (so I fixed it in the games audio menu). The announcer and shopkeeper voice actors were a nice touch, kudos to them. Not sure how much more of this I intend to play. The game is fun ...until it isn't anymore. The roguelite aspect of it succeeds at first, but at some point it's just too much of the same thing over and over. I do not understand the mixed reviews. This TD game is well ahead of the genre. - Solid progression system -Varied towers and spells, each with their own skill trees (and prestige system for towers at least) -Rewarding combos -Small dev group but deeper yet functional difficulty grind, more polished than I anticipated I am not sure I understand the complaints over the egg grind being capped. I find the egg hatching to be fair timing between every few runs. While some builds may be better over others, that is what content balancing patches are for (and also play what is more enjoyable in your runs). I highly recommend this game for TD fans. The price is fair even at full price.
